llm-dlc/loops/stub-reachability.md's step 1. The gap preflight counts a stub as entered when JBMC's symbolic execution alone keeps a step of it. For VF-015's proof (prove Hex#toDigit --assume 'ch == 1632' on commons-codec's old Hex), that counts String.format(String, Object[]) as entered on toDigit's exception path, which the assumption makes infeasible. The new verification/triage/stub-reachability.sh reruns that proof unchanged, with JBMC behind a wrapper that records each command and its time. On the proof's harness and command it then tries two methods. (A) --cover location in place of --unwinding-assertions, reading the goals of DecoderException's constructor, of the stub and of toDigit, and once more with --property on one goal. (B) The proof as given, with a rewritten DecoderException whose String.format call first calls a probe that fails an assertion of its own (throw new AssertionError(), as GapIntrinsics.open). Both also run on a control, the same prove without --assume, where the call is reachable. The job's description gives the outcome each method is expected to have.

Checked inline: the script's syntax, its argv rewriting on made-up commands, and its recording wrapper with echo in place of JBMC. No JBMC was run. The brief's Progress records why the probe is a rewritten caller and not a rewritten goto program: jbmc 6.11 can't write a goto binary for goto-instrument. jbmc --help lists --cover only in --unwinding-assertions' line, so whether --cover is accepted is for the job to show.

### Stub reachability, step 3: the gap preflight asks JBMC's solver, by a probe at each call site, whether a path reaches a stub its symbolic execution enters

Each call site of those stubs (the goto listing's bytecode-index, and the instruction there must call the stub) is rewritten to a method of jvmcontract.StubProbe. The rewrite uses a new shared::redirect_calls_at, which also passes the call site's place. A stub leaves the gaps only when all of its probes hold and so does every unwinding assertion. It joins Found::unreached and the new Found::solved, and the note names why. The stub stays a gap when the run is out of time, gives no verdict or can't be read, or when a call site can't be probed. Preflight::probes records the run. The module doc, lib/README.md's gap section and Preflight::paths' doc describe it.

A placement test covers two stubs in sequence, a call site whose instruction calls another method, and one with no bytecode index. Another test checks the gaps and the note. The live reproducer, a_stub_behind_a_condition_only_the_solver_decides_is_no_gap, is a millisecond JBMC run on the new P.sequenced, like the existing fixture tests.
